description.purpose: One person, as a level. A level owns what its siblings must share, and what two assistants of one person must share is exactly four things: the MEMORY of what was said to that person (memory-hive -- observations, tagged with the participant set they were learned in, raw and carrying a confidence), the RECORD of who that person and their people are (affinity -- curated, fail-closed, quotable), the SCREEN every inbound turn passes (firewall -- deterministic, row-driven, one rate window), and -- since 1.3.0 -- the CHANNELS the person is reached on (GH #454: a chat account, a screen, a phone line). Beside them sit three open containers -- `assistants`, `channels` and, since GH #459, `apps` -- that the person's agents, the person's channels and the person's applications are instantiated into, and, since 1.6.0, no cell of the level's own at all: the one it had, `export-sink`, wrote its holders' exports to disk, and #555 gave every store its own files. The level holds nothing else: no brain, no tools. Since 1.4.0 two more lanes cross this boundary. Outward, `pack_ack` ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)): the receipt of an identity this member's own `./affinity` pushed into one of its generations. The push itself needs no lane here -- producer and consumer are both inside the level, so the edge goes from one sibling to another -- but the receipt has no consumer in here at all, and a level that did not declare it would let a recurring message die as `no_route` at its own boundary. Inward, `in_import` ([#467](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/467)): one part of a memory document, carried by one plain edge onto `./memory-hive`, which has accepted the lane since 2.2.0. It is the SECOND step of a transfer and never the first -- a seed is a file and a `ref` carries none, so a birth still goes through `examples/memory-import/`; this lane is for the hive that is already running. Adding a lane in either direction is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Neither lane grew a new NAME in the same unreleased wave, and two of them grew reach instead: since [#471](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/471) `in_export` fans out to all three holders and `in_import` names one on `hop.import_hive`, and since [#475](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/475) both also reach a FOURTH holder that is not a sibling at all -- the session keeper inside one of this member's generations, addressed through `./assistants` on `context.assistant`, because a member with two generations has two session ledgers and they are not one document. Since 1.5.0 the level carries an `access` occupant (`access@2.5.0`) and the two credential v-lanes a generation's brains spend are drawn onto it by the manifest that grows the generation (GH #560, README section `The credential v-lanes`). A member can now hold its own provider keys, which is something no caller could ask of it before, so it is the second digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 1.5.1 both completeness markers were written the way the table parts already were -- into a neighbour file and renamed over the name a reader watches -- and since 1.6.0 there is neither a cell that writes them nor a member-level marker at all: each holder's own store writes its directory and the marker in it, and the holder says `export_done` for itself ([#563](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/563)). Both repair what the marker already promised, so it is the third digit. Since 1.6.0 the level also carries the mutation receipt into BOTH of its containers, `./assistants` and `./apps` (GH #553): an agent's tool menu and a person's screen are the same fact read twice, and neither asks a timer for it any more.
description.use_when: One instance per person. A group that owns an agent nobody owns personally is a member too, with its own name -- a group is an AUDIENCE, not a holder, so there is no org-level store to put it in. Instantiate it into an org's `members` container and wire its eight inbound and thirteen outbound lanes in the same mutation; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it. Assistants come afterwards, one mutation each, instantiated into ./assistants with their own addressing edges; channels the same way, into ./channels. A second assistant for the same person inherits everything this level already knows -- the memory, the record, the rate window, and since 1.3.0 the CHANNELS as well: one bot, two agents, told apart by name (GH #454). That is the acceptance of GH #122 read one step further, and the reason none of the four is in the agent. Applications the same way, into ./apps: an app produces VIEWS onto a screen of this person and has no port and no surface of its own (GH #459), which is why it belongs beside the agents rather than inside one -- it outlives a generation swap exactly the way a channel does.
description.not_in_scope: No agent and no tool surface: those are the assistant's, and one member may own several. The CHANNELS are no longer among them (GH #454): a bot owned one level down is one agent's bot, a person's second agent cannot be reached through it, and a screen both agents draw on has no owner -- so the channel came up here, where the firewall and the memory already are. No memory-drain -- per-turn extraction (GH #298, ruling Q11) replaced it, and #302 says explicitly it does not belong in the assistant either. No terminal (ruling Q2, GH #284): the refusal lanes leave the level and become no_route in the DLQ if nobody consumes them, which is recorded and self-localising. And since 1.6.0 no cell of its own of any kind: the one it had wrote files for its holders, and #555 gave every store its own. No second identity store and no org-level memory: 'what does the group know about X' is a filter on the read, never a second store. The subscription into a brain is OWNED here and drawn by the mutation that instantiates the level (GH #453, the half GH #302 left open): the record is the member's, a subscription is a row in the record, and an assistant is replaced per generation -- a subscription owned one level down would have to be rewritten on every swap. The record ships one active row at birth, so the push lane carries traffic on the first tick instead of being structurally silent; what it cannot ship is the EDGE, because writing one is a mutation and mutation authority is the colony's. The recipe stays affinity's own and is not restated here. Since 1.2.0 the close pass IS sent from here (GH #447): a closed session's write batch is fanned onto memory-hive's `in_close_pass` as well as out of the level, so the strong model reads the session whole and the answer to 'who fires the close pass' is 'the level that owns the memory'. No APP and no view of its own either (GH #459): the smallest view there is is a prose block, and every agent already has it -- an agent's ordinary `answer`, carried into ./channels by the lane GH #454 drew, IS a view once the channel on the other end is a display. An app is what gets built when the picture is worth code, and it is instantiated into ./apps, never shipped in it.
examples: PORTS - the member is an OPEN hive: it declares no params.ports, because it is a level that gets wired INTO and sealing it would refuse exactly the endpoints an assistant or a channel instantiation needs. Entry lanes, all eight addressed at the member path itself: 'in_turn' -> the screen (promote context.channel -- the chat or room -- plus context.channel_node when the answer is to be routed back into one of this member's own channels, and context.user_id where this colony has per-user firewall rules); 'in_recall' -> this member's memory, turned into the hive's own in_query at the door (send hop.recall_query, hop.memory_tier, hop.recall_window_from, hop.recall_window_to, and the round on context.audience_set + context.channel); 'in_brief' and 'in_propose' -> the record (promote context.asker + context.audience_set for a read, context.actor + context.subscriber for a write); 'in_build_result' -> the generation that asked; 'in_export' -> all three holders at once, which needs no keys at all -- plus, when the caller names a generation on context.assistant, the session keeper inside it (GH #475). Since GH #555 each holder's own STORE writes the seed set, inside the fence it declares in params.transfer.base_path, and hop.export_to names the directory of one run; and 'in_import' -> the holder hop.import_hive names, memory by default, once it is running: ONE export part per message, idempotent, the return leg of in_export and the only way in for everything the source learned after the walk (a seed is read once, at birth -- see examples/memory-import/). Exits, thirteen lanes, all leaving the member path: 'answer' (the brief, told apart from a push by hop.subscriber == '' -- and, since 1.3.0, a turn ANSWERED whose caller named no channel of this member, carried out by a guarded default), 'ack' (a write was accepted or rejected), 'reject' (the screen refused a turn, or the memory refused a question, a block or a walk), 'error' (a failure that was not a refusal, from a holder, from a CHANNEL or from an assistant), 'close_report' (what the close pass did to an ended session), 'export_done' (a holder wrote its own seed set and says where -- three per export, four when a generation was named; GH #555), 'dump' (the receipt of one applied import part, from whichever holder took it), 'build' (a structural wish leaving a generation), 'pack_ack' (the receipt of an identity pack, from a generation this member's own record pushed to), 'bundle' (since GH #533: the answer to a question sent at the 'in_recall' door, guarded on the reply-to token this level stamps at that door -- every other bundle goes DOWN into the generation that asked, on the default edge, exactly as before), and the three an assistant raises that this level does not stop: 'write' and, since GH #527, 'turn_write' -- both FANNED, out AND down into the memory hive (the close pass for one, the episode lane for the other) -- plus 'prune', which nothing here consumes at all. The refusal and receipt lanes MUST be drained by the parent, or they dead-letter as no_route.

the containers: ./assistants and ./channels are real, empty, open hives. ./assistants -- IN: in_turn (the screened turn coming back from the screen, carrying context.assistant) and in_bundle (the memory's answer), plus answer coming back the other way is not an in-lane of it but of ./channels. OUT, the eight of the assistant level: answer, write, turn_write, extraction, recall, prune, error, build. The member consumes four itself (answer at ./channels, recall and extraction at ./memory-hive, write additionally fanned onto the close pass) and re-emits the rest on its own contract; since GH #527 turn_write is fanned the same way write is -- out on the contract AND down onto the hive's in_episode lane, which is the only path in the substrate from a conversation into an episodes table. ./channels -- IN from a channel: turn and error. OUT to a channel: answer. The lists are derived from templates/assistant/config.json at the tree, and crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh302_member_holds_the_memory.rs reads both files so a lane that moves in the assistant moves here in the same commit.

the unbound behaviour of ./assistants is UNDECLARED, deliberately: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared word could never fire. A message that reaches it before an assistant is instantiated takes the ordinary path. The measurement comes from unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope.

one person, two agents, ONE channel: instantiate member once, then two assistants into ./assistants and one channel into ./channels. The second agent starts knowing what the member knows -- same memory, same record, same rate window on the same attacker -- and is reachable on the same bot, by name. Nothing is copied and nothing is synchronised, because there was only ever one of each. That is what GH #454 bought and what crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh454_two_assistants_one_channel.rs measures.

the write half of the memory is one edge: ./assistants -> ./memory-hive on hop.route == 'extraction', re-stamped to in_remember. It is here rather than in the agent because the memory belongs to the MEMBER (GH #122, ADR 0012), and the second edge of talky's two-edge recipe -- the hive's reject egress -- is the ./memory-hive -> . lane this level already ships.

the close pass is one edge and no new cell (GH #447): ./assistants -> ./memory-hive on hop.route == 'write', re-stamped to in_close_pass and promoting session_id, audience_set and channel. It is a FAN-OUT rather than a redirection -- the same close batch still leaves the level on 'write' for whatever archive the parent wired, because the two readers want different things from it. The receipt comes back on close_report and leaves the level; the member triggers the pass and is not its reader.

the export is four edges and no cell at all: . -> ./memory-hive, . -> ./affinity and . -> ./firewall on in_export start three walks, . -> ./assistants starts a fourth when the caller named a generation on context.assistant (GH #475), and since GH #555 each holder's OWN store writes <hive>/seed/<table>.jsonl inside the fence it declares in params.transfer.base_path, with <hive>/seed/export_final.json written last -- the holder that finished says export_done itself, naming the directory. One PLAIN hop.route == 'export_done' edge per holder carries it out, and one PLAIN hop.route == 'dump' edge per holder carries the receipt of an applied import part. Neither edge may test a second hop key: every one of those hives runs a required_drains probe that puts the described hop through the real edge evaluator, and an edge guarded on a key the probe does not describe evaluates false and reads as no drain at all.

channels, since 1.3.0 (GH #454): ./channels is a real, empty, open hive beside ./assistants. One channel is one node in it, named for what `context.channel_node` will say -- `telegram`, `slack`, `display-<screen>`, `voice` -- and two edges: the channel's raw wire up to the container on `turn`, and the container down to the channel on `answer` guarded by `context.channel_node == '<name>'`. Since GH #522 the ingress edge promotes TWO keys: `context.channel_node`, the node name the answer is routed back by, and `context.channel`, the CHAT (`has(hop.chat_id) ? hop.chat_id : ''`) that the session keeper opens a generation for, the firewall rate-limits and the memory writes down as the room. One word could not be both -- keyed on the node name, every chat of one connector shared one generation, one bucket and one room. A screen carries the same word in both, because a screen is one room. The level ships the rest: `./channels -> ./firewall` re-stamps `turn` to `in_turn` with the same channel promotion the outside door uses, `./assistants -> ./channels` carries the answer back when `context.channel_node` names a channel, `./assistants -> .` carries it OUT as a guarded default when it does not, and `./channels -> .` lets a connector's own failure leave on the level's error lane.

ADDRESSING one of two assistants through one channel (GH #454, rule v1): the channel's own outbound edge stamps `context.assistant` with the name of the agent the message was meant for -- from an address rule of the channel (a prefix or a mention the connector parsed onto a hop key) or, when the message names nobody, from the channel's own default, written as a literal in that edge. No model decides it. The container then fans out: one edge `./assistants -> ./assistants/<name>` per assistant, guarded on `context.assistant == '<name>'`. Edge targets are static in this substrate (`Edge.to` is a path), so there is no single edge that means 'whatever the context says' -- a new assistant is one more edge per direction, and that is the documented cost.

the display channel is BUILT, since GH #459: `./channels/display-<screen>` holds a `display@1.0.2` and is wired like any other channel -- `event` and `receipt` up, `answer` and `view` down, the down-edge re-stamping both to the display's own `in_view`. It is a screen of the PERSON, which is why two of their agents may hold views on it at once. A screen costs TWO edges and not the chat channel's three: a connector's third edge catches `hop.error_code`, and a display emits no such thing -- its contract declares `event` and `receipt` and nothing else, and a receipt carries its `error_code` in the BODY. An error edge here would have no producer, so it is not drawn (see templates/member/README.md, 'The display channel').

apps, since GH #459: ./apps is a real, empty, open hive beside ./assistants and ./channels. An APP is a specific composition and specific code out of a build order -- a derived template in the library tagged `app` -- instantiated here as `apps/<name>`. It has NO PORT: it writes views onto a screen of this member, and whatever authentication stands in front of that screen stands in front of it. TRANSIT: `view` and `error` up, `event` and `receipt` down. The level ships `./apps -> ./channels` on `view` (guarded on a non-empty context.channel_node, because an app is display-blind and the screen is named in the edge that LEAVES the app), `./apps -> .` on error, and the two owner-guarded edges back down.

the way back from a screen is the OWNER and nothing else (GH #459): the display stamps `hop.owner` -- the path of the cell whose `reply_to` put the view up -- and `hop.view_id` beside it, on `event` and on `receipt`. It has to be the HOP: an edge condition reads `context.*` and `hop.*` and never the body (crates/meclaw-colony/src/cel_eval.rs, bind_ctx). This level splits on the CONTAINER -- `hop.owner.contains('/assistants/')` becomes `in_turn` with `hop.kind` set to `event` or `receipt` (the assistant level has no event lane and did not grow one; `in_turn` is what it accepts and the header says what kind of turn it is), `contains('/apps/')` keeps the lane name, and anything else leaves on `error` with the original lane on `hop.kind`. It is `contains` and not a prefix because the owner is an ABSOLUTE path and a template does not know its own. Which agent and which app stays the mutation's edge, the same static-`Edge.to` cost GH #454 documented.
